#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from PBS

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# PBS resources:
#   -N BUSCO
#   -P xl04
#   -q normalsr
#   -l walltime=20:00:00
#   -l mem=512GB
#   -l ncpus=104
#   -j oe
#   -l storage=gdata/xl04+gdata/if89
#   -l wd
#   -l jobfs=100GB
#   -M kirat.alreja@anu.edu.au

#flux: --job-name=BUSCO
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 104
#flux: --time-limit=20h

# Omitted PBS option: -l mem=512GB
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted PBS option: -P xl04 (project/account)
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default project/account or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted PBS option: -q normalsr (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different limits/priority or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted PBS option: -j oe (join stdout/stderr)
# Flux commonly manages stdout/stderr separately; a portable join directive is not guaranteed.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but logs may be split.

# Omitted PBS options: -l storage=... and -l jobfs=100GB
# These are site-specific storage directives with no portable Flux equivalents.
# Performance implication: required filesystems/scratch may not be provisioned, causing I/O failures or slower performance.

# Omitted PBS option: -M kirat.alreja@anu.edu.au (email)
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

module load singularity

# NOTE: PBS -l wd changes to the submission directory; under Flux we stay in the directory where flux batch is invoked.

lineage=/g/data/xl04/bpadata/Bassiana_duperreyi/projects/chromsyn/busco_downloads

# `fasta` and `outpath` are referenced but not defined in the original script; assume they are exported by the user.
# Performance implication: if not set, the job will fail immediately.

prefix=$(basename "${fasta}" .fasta)
cd "${outpath}"

# PBS variable $PBS_NCPUS is not set under Flux; use allocated cores (104).
singularity exec /g/data/xl04/ka6418/docker_images/busco-5.4.7.sif \
  busco -o "run_${prefix}" --offline -i "$fasta" -l sauropsida_odb10 \
  --download_path "$lineage" --cpu 104 -m genome --tar

reasons: PBS requested 512GB of memory (`-l mem=512GB`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.

PBS specified a queue and project/account (`-q normalsr`, `-P xl04`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/account selection; on sites where these affect eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.

PBS specified required storage/jobfs resources (`-l storage=...`, `-l jobfs=100GB`) but the Flux resource section has no equivalent storage constraints; required filesystems/scratch may not be provisioned.
